newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill upgrades BIG to "buy" rating.
newsitem.headline: Merrill upgrades BIG to "buy" rating.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has upgraded to buy its neutral intermediate-term rating and accumulate long-term rating for Polish bank BIG after its recent fall along with the Warsaw bourse, Merrill said in a report.
"We are raising our intermediate and long-term opinion on BIG shares to Buy," the report dated October 29 said.

Merrill said that shares in BIG, whose full name is Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA, and the main market's WIG index had both lost 13 percent of their value since September 30, though there had been no fundamental reason for BIG's fall.
In an earlier report dated October 16 Merrill Lynch maintained its neutral intermediate rating for BIG but said the stock was a good long-term buy.

"The shares now trade 25 percent below our year-end 1996 price objective of PLN 4.4 and...offer over 40 percent upside in USD terms relative to our 1997 share price objective of PLN 5.8," the report said.
It said the 40 percent figure would apply even assuming a 22-percent devaluation of the zloty relative to the dollar over the next 14 months.

Merrill said BIG traded at 5.2 times estimated 1996 earnings and 4.2 times estimated 1997 earnings, representing a 32-percent discount to the average 1996 and 1997 price-earnings ratios of Slaski, BRE and BPH.
BIG closed on Wednesday at 3.7 zlotys
